scope_plain: Voters in Congressional District 3, which includes all of Allen (the district drawn in 2025)
office_explainer: Your voice in the U.S. House: votes on federal laws, taxes and spending.
why_it_matters: Keith Self, a former Collin County judge, holds this seat and is seeking another two-year term.

candidates.name: Keith Self
candidates.background: Holds this seat; retired Army officer (25 years, after West Point) and Collin County judge from 2007 to 2018 (House website; Dallas Morning News). Did not answer the LWV questionnaire.

own_words.text: I have voted against $3.5 trillion in spending bills, not because they are bad bills, but because they proposed spending money on things that are not priorities for the American people.
Congress has several options: request reports on war progress, declare war, pass a relevant Authorization for Use of Military Force (AUMF).
I have advocated for local control of those decisions because the federal government should not dictate to local communities who can do business there.

candidates.name: Evan Hunt
candidates.background: Retired Air Force lieutenant colonel who served as a B-1 weapons systems officer; now an aerospace and defense business development executive; University of Pennsylvania graduate; has not held office (campaign site; Dallas Morning News).

own_words.text: My goal is to move the federal government as close to a balanced budget as responsibly possible, without breaking our commitments to Social Security and Medicare or compromising national security.
Congress should debate and vote on continued military action in the region rather than allowing an open-ended conflict to continue without clear authorization.
Our biggest challenge is managing explosive growth without sacrificing affordability and quality of life.

Opposes expanding Medicaid "under Obamacare"; wants a "Texas Solution" that covers uninsured Texans and keeps protections for pre-existing conditions.

own_words.text: I utilize AI-assisted software to automate administrative bottlenecks like data entry and scheduling.

candidates.name: Irvin Lynn Barrett
candidates.background: Senior pastor, hospice chaplain and insurance agent; studied at Criswell College (LWV guide; Ballotpedia). Did not answer the Dallas Morning News questionnaire.

own_words.text: Justice of Peace court is where everyday people meet the justice system for the first time. It may be the only encounter they ever have with the judicial system. This encounter should not be threatening or intimidating.

office_explainer: One of three elected directors on the board that oversees the office that sets property values for taxes.
why_it_matters: Nonpartisan: no party labels. Texas first elected some appraisal district directors in May 2024, under a 2023 law (Senate Bill 2); this is the first time these seats are on a November ballot. The appraisal district's own page says its board has no authority to set values; it hires the chief appraiser, adopts the budget and reappraisal plan, and appoints the Appraisal Review Board. A winner needs more than half the votes, or the top two go to a runoff. After this election, the three winners draw lots: one serves two years and two serve four.
